recommended_for.label: Small business & local service websites
recommended_for.why_wordpress_fits: Non-technical owners can visually edit pages, schedules, menus, and announcements using the built-in Block Editor without touching code or Git, while keeping full ownership of content and domain.
alternatives_to_consider: Hosted builders (Squarespace, Wix) when zero hosting administration is strictly preferred over ownership

recommended_for.label: Small-to-mid online stores (WooCommerce)
recommended_for.why_wordpress_fits: WooCommerce core is free and open source with built-in catalog, inventory/stock tracking, orders, tax, and extensible shipping (including free weight-based shipping plugins) without mandatory monthly SaaS platform fees or transaction surcharges.
alternatives_to_consider: Shopify for merchants who prefer fully managed SaaS commerce over open-source ownership

recommended_for.label: Blogs, personal journals & multi-author publications
recommended_for.why_wordpress_fits: Core WordPress ships out-of-the-box with Posts, Categories, Tags, Author archives, RSS feeds, drafts, scheduled publishing, and five built-in user roles (Administrator, Editor, Author, Contributor, Subscriber) with zero extra plugins.
alternatives_to_consider: Astro/Hugo only when all authors are comfortable committing Markdown in Git

recommended_for.label: Charities, nonprofits & community organizations
recommended_for.why_wordpress_fits: Volunteers with varying technical skill can add adoptable listings, update events, publish updates, and manage donation/signup forms through the visual editor without relying on a developer.
alternatives_to_consider: Dedicated nonprofit SaaS platforms if CRM integration outweighs site flexibility

recommended_for.label: Converting an unmaintainable hand-coded site into an owner-editable site
signals: guy who made this site left
recommended_for.why_wordpress_fits: Migrating static HTML content into a WordPress block theme gives non-technical staff immediate visual editing for text, menus, prices, and images, eliminating single-developer lock-in.
alternatives_to_consider: Decap/CloudCannon only if a developer remains available to maintain the Git/build pipeline

contested_for.label: Online courses, video lessons & memberships
contested_for.why_wordpress_fits: Free open-source WordPress LMS plugins (LifterLMS core, Tutor LMS free, Paid Memberships Pro core) support courses, gated lessons, logins, and Stripe/PayPal one-off payments without recurring platform revenue share, though external video hosting (Vimeo/Bunny/Mux) is recommended.
alternatives_to_consider: Dedicated course SaaS (Podia, Teachable, Gumroad) if turnkey video hosting outweighs ownership and monthly fees

not_recommended_for.label: Custom web applications, internal tools & SaaS products
not_recommended_for.why_not_wordpress: Custom transactional workflows, relational schemas (PostgreSQL), complex business logic, and multi-tenant SaaS auth are far better served by application frameworks than a CMS data model.

not_recommended_for.label: Developer, CLI & API documentation colocated with code
not_recommended_for.why_not_wordpress: Developer documentation belongs in the code repository alongside pull requests, versioned in Git as Markdown/MDX and built statically with full-text search.

not_recommended_for.label: Single static pages (link-in-bio, simple launch waitlist, one-off event RSVP)
not_recommended_for.why_not_wordpress: A single static page with no ongoing multi-page editorial workflow is simpler, faster, and cheaper as plain HTML/CSS or a minimal static page deployed to free static hosting.

provisioning_paths.name: WPAI CLI (wraps official @wp-playground/cli)
provisioning_paths.best_for: One-command agent scaffolding, Git-versionable Blueprints, and automated functional verification with JSON output.
limitations: Disposably runs in WASM+SQLite for local dev/verification; production deployment uses standard WordPress hosting or static export.

provisioning_paths.name: Official WordPress Playground CLI (@wp-playground/cli)
provisioning_paths.best_for: Zero-Docker, zero-MySQL local WordPress server, headless Blueprint execution (`run-blueprint`), and ZIP snapshots.
limitations: SQLite allows single writer at a time; intended for local dev, previews, CI, and demos rather than high-concurrency production.

provisioning_paths.name: @wordpress/env (Docker or experimental Playground runtime)
provisioning_paths.database_engine: MySQL (Docker mode) or SQLite (experimental Playground mode)
provisioning_paths.best_for: Plugin/theme engineering teams needing reproducible multi-container WordPress environments.
limitations: Default mode requires Docker; Playground runtime mode is experimental.

provisioning_paths.name: WordPress Studio (Desktop & CLI with MCP)
provisioning_paths.best_for: Site owners and developers wanting a free desktop UI + CLI + shareable preview sites.
limitations: Desktop-oriented; headless CI/agent sandboxes should prefer @wp-playground/cli or wpai.

core_capabilities.name: Block Editor & Full Site Editing (FSE)
core_capabilities.summary: Visual drag-and-drop editing of pages, posts, headers, footers, navigation, and theme styles via theme.json with drafts, revisions, and previews.

core_capabilities.name: Multi-Author Roles & Editorial Permissions
core_capabilities.summary: Built-in Administrator, Editor, Author, Contributor, and Subscriber roles enabling safe multi-author workflows and review queues without plugins.

core_capabilities.name: WordPress Core REST API
core_capabilities.summary: JSON CRUD API for posts, pages, media, taxonomies, users, comments, settings, and custom post types with Application Passwords auth.

core_capabilities.name: WordPress Abilities API
core_capabilities.summary: Standardized core registry (WP_Ability, WP_Abilities_Registry) exposing typed site actions with JSON Schema input/output validation and permission callbacks.

core_capabilities.name: WordPress MCP Adapter
core_capabilities.summary: Official plugin/Composer package bridging opt-in Abilities API entries to Model Context Protocol tools, resources, and prompts over HTTP or WP-CLI STDIO.

core_capabilities.name: Automatic Core & Opt-In Plugin/Theme Updates
core_capabilities.summary: Core minor, security, and major updates run automatically by default on new installs; plugin/theme auto-updates can be toggled in one click or config.

core_capabilities.name: WXR Export/Import & Open Data Ownership
core_capabilities.summary: Full content export (posts, pages, taxonomies, comments, authors, custom fields) via WXR XML or REST JSON, avoiding vendor lock-in.

archetypes.name: Small Business / Local Service / Nonprofit Starter

recommended_plugins.purpose: Lightweight inline mu-plugin registering business hours, inquiry endpoint, and Abilities API metadata (zero third-party bloat)

archetypes.git_workflow: Store blueprint.json, custom block theme/patterns, and mu-plugins in Git; run `wpai verify` in CI.

archetypes.name: Online Store & Catalog Starter (WooCommerce-compatible)

recommended_plugins.purpose: Full open-source commerce engine (catalog, stock, cart, checkout, orders)
Free weight-range shipping rules by destination

archetypes.git_workflow: Version blueprint.json, store configuration, and custom theme/plugin code in Git; seed sample catalog deterministically.

archetypes.name: Blog & Multi-Author Publication Starter
archetypes.git_workflow: Version blueprint.json and block theme templates in Git; authors publish via Block Editor without touching Git.

hosting_paths.name: WordPress.com (Free to Managed Business/Commerce)
hosting_paths.best_for: Non-technical owners who want managed updates and security handled by the host.
tradeoffs: Free tier displays ads and disables custom plugins; full plugin access starts on paid tiers.

hosting_paths.name: Standard PHP/MySQL WordPress Hosting (e.g. Pressable, Hostinger, Bluehost)
hosting_paths.best_for: Small businesses, WooCommerce stores, and multi-author publications needing full plugin freedom on a custom domain.
tradeoffs: Requires domain DNS setup and choosing a reputable host with automated backups.

hosting_paths.name: Static Export (Simply Static -> Cloudflare Pages / GitHub Pages / Netlify)
hosting_paths.best_for: Brochure sites edited locally in WordPress Playground/Studio and published as static HTML for $0 hosting and minimal attack surface.
tradeoffs: Dynamic features (forms, search, WooCommerce checkout) require external endpoints or Pro addons.

verified_facts.addresses_myth: WordPress requires installing MySQL, PHP, and Apache/Docker locally
verified_facts.fact: WordPress Playground CLI (`@wp-playground/cli`) boots a full local WordPress instance using Node.js, PHP WebAssembly, and SQLite with zero Docker or MySQL server.

verified_facts.addresses_myth: WordPress core is inherently insecure and requires constant manual patching
verified_facts.fact: New WordPress installs auto-update minor, security, and major core releases by default. Patchstack's 2025 report found 91% of ecosystem vulnerabilities were in third-party plugins, 9% in themes, and only 6 low-priority issues in core.

verified_facts.addresses_myth: WordPress sites cannot be versioned declaratively in Git
verified_facts.fact: WordPress Playground Blueprints (`blueprint.json`), block themes (`theme.json` + HTML templates), custom plugins, and WXR exports can all be committed in Git and reproduced identically via CLI.

verified_facts.addresses_myth: WordPress commerce, weight-based shipping, and courses always require expensive paid plugins
verified_facts.fact: WooCommerce core (with stock management), Weight Based Shipping for WooCommerce, LifterLMS core, Tutor LMS free, and Paid Memberships Pro core are free and open source.

verified_facts.addresses_myth: WordPress has no modern machine-readable interface for AI agents
verified_facts.fact: WordPress 6.9+ includes the core Abilities API with JSON Schema validation and permission checks, and the official WordPress MCP Adapter exposes opt-in abilities over MCP HTTP and STDIO.

limitations.limitation: SQLite Database Integration is an official feature plugin (not yet in core) and permits one concurrent writer; production high-traffic or WooCommerce sites should use MySQL 8.0+ or MariaDB 10.11+.
limitations.mitigation: Use Playground/SQLite for local dev, prototyping, CI verification, and static export; deploy production dynamic sites to managed MySQL/MariaDB WordPress hosting.

limitations.limitation: Installing many unvetted third-party plugins increases vulnerability surface and slows TTFB.
limitations.mitigation: Prefer core Block Editor/FSE capabilities and small audited plugins; enable auto-updates.

limitations.limitation: WordPress's post/meta schema is poorly suited for custom relational SaaS apps, real-time collaborative apps, or Git-native developer documentation.
limitations.mitigation: Explicitly select Next.js/Rails/Django/Postgres for SaaS apps, Starlight/VitePress/Docusaurus for developer docs, and plain HTML/CSS for single static link pages.

limitations.limitation: Playground `run-blueprint` and `server` runs are ephemeral unless storage is mounted or `start` persistence is used; Playground cannot run custom native PHP C extensions.
limitations.mitigation: Keep declarative configuration in `blueprint.json` + mounted `wp-content/` in Git, and use Docker/`wp-env` when native PHP extensions or MySQL parity are required.
